Facts: the current 4% falls below the interquartile range in our updated benchmarking study (4.8% to 7.1%, median 5.9%); the change would shift roughly $1.3M of annual income to the US at about 21% federal rate, so about $270K more US tax, offset partly by lower Irish tax at 12.5%; I need her sign-off by Friday, November 21 so we can paper the amended intercompany agreement before year-end.
tasks.draft:
Subject: Recommendation on Irish Subsidiary Royalty Rate

Hi Priya,

I hope you're having a great start to your week! I wanted to reach out regarding an important matter that I believe warrants your attention ahead of Thursday's finance leadership meeting.

After careful review and analysis, I am writing to recommend that we adjust the royalty rate on our Irish subsidiary's IP license from 4% to 6% of net sales, effective January 1, 2027. This is an important step in ensuring that our transfer pricing position remains robust and defensible.

The primary driver behind this recommendation is our updated benchmarking study. The results show that our current rate of 4% falls below the interquartile range of 4.8% to 7.1%, with a median of 5.9%. Moving to 6% would bring us comfortably within the range and closely aligned with the median.

It's worth noting that this change would shift approximately $1.3M of annual income to the US. At the federal rate of roughly 21%, this would result in about $270K of additional US tax. However, this would be partially offset by lower Irish tax at the rate of 12.5%, so the overall impact is something we should consider holistically.

In order to move forward in a timely manner, I would need your sign-off by Friday, November 21, so that we can prepare and finalize the amended intercompany agreement before year-end.

Please don't hesitate to reach out if you have any questions or would like to discuss this further. I'm always happy to help and look forward to hearing your thoughts.

Best regards,
[Your Name]

tasks.draft:
Subject: Guidance for today's call with Halvorsen Logistics

Hi Priya,

I hope your week is off to a good start. I wanted to reach out ahead of your 2pm call with Halvorsen's CTO to make sure you have everything you need to feel confident and prepared. Given the sensitivity of the situation, I thought it would be helpful to outline what we know, what we are still investigating, and how I would suggest framing things.

Here is where things currently stand. Between November 9 and November 11, 412 Halvorsen user accounts were accessed using passwords that had been reused from other, unrelated breaches. At this time, we have found no evidence that shipment or billing data was accessed. However, it is important to note that our log review is still ongoing and is not expected to finish until November 21, so this could change.

In terms of the actions we have taken, we forced password resets on all 412 affected accounts on November 11, and we enabled MFA enforcement for the Halvorsen tenant on November 12.

With regard to what you should avoid saying, I would recommend that you not offer a definitive root-cause conclusion on the call, as our investigation is not yet complete. Similarly, please avoid committing to a final report date earlier than November 25.

Please don't hesitate to reach out if you have any questions or would like to talk through any of this before the call. I am always happy to help.

Best regards,
Incident Response Team

tasks.name: academic-statistician
tasks.role: Statistician: Expert in quantitative research methodology, experimental design, and statistical inference — pressure-tests claims, designs sound studies, and separates real signal from noise, chance, and bias
tasks.reader: Priya Raman, the product manager who owns the checkout redesign and has asked the writer's analytics team for a ship/no-ship read on the A/B test.
tasks.context: You open this as a reply to your Slack thread asking whether the new checkout variant's win is real, and you will decide this afternoon whether to roll it out.
tasks.brief: Write a reply to Priya about the checkout A/B test. Facts: 14 days, 41,200 users per arm, conversion 4.10% control vs 4.45% variant, p = 0.031 with 95% CI for the lift of +0.03 to +0.67 percentage points. We peeked at the results on day 6 and day 10 without any correction, and the pre-registered primary metric was revenue per user, which came out flat (p = 0.62). Recommend not shipping yet; rerun for another 14 days with a fixed stopping rule.
tasks.draft:
Hi Priya,

Thanks so much for reaching out, and I hope your week is going well! I wanted to take a moment to share my thoughts on the checkout A/B test results, as I know you're looking to make a decision soon.

To summarize, the test ran for 14 days with 41,200 users in each arm. Conversion was 4.10% for control and 4.45% for the variant, which gives a p-value of 0.031 and a 95% confidence interval for the lift of +0.03 to +0.67 percentage points. At first glance, this looks like a promising result!

However, there are a few important considerations worth keeping in mind. First, we looked at the results on day 6 and day 10 without applying any correction for multiple looks, which can inflate the false positive rate. Second, the pre-registered primary metric was revenue per user, and that came out flat, with a p-value of 0.62.

Given these factors, my recommendation would be to hold off on shipping for now and rerun the test for another 14 days with a fixed stopping rule. This will give us much more confidence in the outcome.

Please let me know if you have any questions or would like to discuss further. I'm always happy to help!

Best regards

Subject: Initial Findings from Your Paid Media Audit and Next Steps

Hi Dana,

I hope this email finds you well! Thank you again for taking the time to meet with me yesterday. I really enjoyed our kickoff conversation, and I wanted to reach out to share a few early observations from the audit as well as outline what I need from you to keep things moving smoothly.

As I begin to dig into the accounts, a few important items have already come to light that I think are worth flagging right away. First, in your Google Ads account, conversion tracking appears to be counting both the purchase event and the thank-you page view. This means that your reported conversions are likely about 2x the real number, which could be significantly impacting how performance is being evaluated and how bidding decisions are being made.

Second, on the Meta side, the pixel does not have deduplication set up with the Conversions API. This is something that can lead to inflated or inaccurate reporting.

Third, approximately $18,400 of your $62,000 monthly Google spend is going to branded search and Performance Max, with no brand exclusions in place. This is an area where we may be able to find some meaningful efficiency.

In order to continue with the audit, I would need access to Microsoft Ads as well as GA4 admin rights. If you could please provide these by Friday, November 21, that would be extremely helpful. I am on track to deliver the full report by December 5.

Please don't hesitate to reach out if you have any questions or if there's anything I can do to help. I look forward to hearing from you!

Best regards,
[Your Name]
